title: Consolidate core governance domain model
rawUserRequest: Complete the remaining governed Work Items. WI-18 must unify WorkItem, Contract, Evidence, Receipt, Decision, Transition, Finding, Risk, HumanDecision, CapabilityClaim, and Closure; scripts must not independently reinterpret lifecycle states.

rawRequestSource.reference: AI Cockpit comprehensive remediation instructions, WI-18; active user goal

declaredIntent.summary: Make lifecycle facts and transitions typed, centrally validated, and reusable without silently changing the existing lifecycle contract.

outOfScope: Provider configuration, repository branch protection, external identity, release, and production operations.
Historical archived Work Item records and unrelated script-by-script schema migrations.

sources.reason: Existing canonical lifecycle state evaluator to preserve behind the shared domain service.
Existing append-only evidence vocabulary that the core Evidence and Finding objects must not contradict.
Current public lifecycle and recovery behavior to retain and clarify.

riskAssessment.reason: A central model can accidentally alter lifecycle legality or evidence requirements; compatibility adapters and fail-closed tests are required.

reasons: Lifecycle state and evidence interpretation are repository governance boundaries that require full verification.

override.approvalEvidence: User authorized governed Contract and Work Item writes in this thread.
override.reason: Strict lifecycle and evidence review without a release operation.
notRunChecks: Release-preflight and distribution checks are not applicable because no release-owned resource or operation is touched.

executionDecision.reason: The work is limited to repository-local typed models, compatibility adapter, tests, and documentation; no provider or production operation is requested.

preReviewWarnings: Preserve exact current transition outcomes and evidence gates; do not claim that unrelated scripts are globally migrated.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A single typed domain module defines WorkItem, Contract, Evidence, Receipt, Decision, Transition, Finding, Risk, HumanDecision, CapabilityClaim, and Closure without duplicated lifecycle-state vocabulary.
The domain service exclusively decides canonical lifecycle transition legality, matching evidence kind, idempotency, and fail-closed stale or contradictory evidence behavior.
The existing ai_work_item_state CLI remains a compatibility adapter whose valid and invalid outputs match the previous externally observable contract.
Tests reject illegal transitions and malformed evidence through the domain service and prove the adapter delegates to it.
The state-machine reference documents the domain-service authority and the limited compatibility boundary.
guidelines: Keep lifecycle state, evidence kind, and transition decisions owned by the shared domain model rather than re-declaring them in adapters.
Preserve append-only evidence and fail-closed behavior; do not weaken existing transition checks.
Do not modify provider configuration or historical archived Work Items.

intent.problem: The repository has a deterministic Work Item state evaluator, an event-evidence vocabulary, and several governance record shapes, but no explicit shared domain model for the core objects. This invites future scripts to re-interpret lifecycle states and evidence differently.
constraints: Preserve existing lifecycle CLI and valid transition semantics.
Reject illegal transitions and stale, contradictory, or malformed evidence fail closed.
Keep the migration bounded to the lifecycle adapter; do not claim every historical script is rewritten.
Do not modify provider configuration, release behavior, or archived Work Items.
intent.rationale: A compact typed domain vocabulary plus one authoritative transition service makes future consumers reuse the same legal-state and evidence rules while retaining a stable compatibility boundary.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A canonical lifecycle step with matching digest-bound evidence is accepted by the domain service.
scenarioCoverage.expected: accepted transition and deterministic receipt identity
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add domain-model unit tests and retain the existing state-machine regression suite.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A skipped, unknown, stale, contradictory, or locally/remote-inconsistent transition is rejected uniformly.
scenarioCoverage.expected: allowed=false with an actionable resume condition
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Parametrized domain-service tests cover illegal order and every invalid evidence signal.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The legacy CLI adapter returns the same external JSON fields while delegating its decision to the domain service.
scenarioCoverage.expected: stable CLI payload for valid and invalid transitions
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Existing CLI regression plus an adapter-delegation test.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Typed evidence and findings cannot become a success state when their required identity or digest is malformed.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Domain-model validation tests for missing identifiers and evidence digest.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: User authorized governed Contract and Work Item writes.

humanDecisionPoints: Before merge, a reviewer confirms that the bounded adapter migration preserves lifecycle compatibility and does not overclaim a repository-wide rewrite.
requiredEvidence: Full governed verification and hosted PR checks.
rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff to restore the previous adapter implementation; no external state is changed.
